claims.text: The proposed starting material is a cast eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The intervention creates a hierarchical microstructure combining lamellar and equiaxed grains.
A mixed lamellar-and-equiaxed hierarchical microstructure can simultaneously increase strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
A lamellar FCC/B2 eutectic microstructure can provide a combination of high fracture strength and high tensile ductility at room temperature.
The hierarchical lamellar-and-equiaxed microstructure facilitates dislocation transmission.
The hierarchical lamellar-and-equiaxed microstructure relieves stress concentrations.
Facilitated dislocation transmission and relief of stress concentrations lead to improved strength and ductility.
The intervention will increase strength by 20% relative to a conventional eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform microstructure.
The intervention will increase ductility by 30% relative to a conventional eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform microstructure.
The strength-ductility benefit should occur at room temperature.
The hierarchical microstructure remains effective at elevated temperatures up to 700 °C.
Failure to obtain at least a 15% strength increase and a 25% ductility increase relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted improvement is 20% in strength and 30% in ductility, whereas the falsification rule uses lower thresholds of 15% and 25%. Outcomes between these thresholds would miss the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
